sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Biocompatible Dental Ceramic Blocks and Milling Discs

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended by Ley No. 4 de 2010; correlative provisions of the Código Civil and Registro Público regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública / Acta Constitutiva (Foundation Charter), formalized before a Panamanian Notary and recorded in the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for Private Interest Foundations under Panama law; however, the Foundation Charter must declare an initial endowment (patrimonio inicial) of at least USD 10,000. This amount does not require placement in a public escrow; it is evidenced by a written subscription certificate and remains under the administration of the Foundation Council.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that this Private Interest Foundation accepts the initial endowment of USD 10,000 subscribed by the Founder, as reflected in the Foundation Charter; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Foundation shall be located at the address specified in the Charter, and the same is adopted as the Foundation's legal domicile; RESOLVED, that the following individuals are appointed as members of the Foundation Council, and the offices of President, Secretary, and Treasurer are hereby designated; RESOLVED, that the Council is authorized to open corporate bank accounts, execute manufacturing contracts, and obtain all industrial, sanitary, municipal, and environmental licenses necessary for the production of dental zirconia ceramic blocks; and RESOLVED, that these resolutions take immediate effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Panamanian attorney to draft the Foundation Charter. The Founder and initial Foundation Council members must appear before the Notary, provide valid identification, and execute the document. Notarized copies are then prepared for registry submission.
required_dossiers: Foundation Charter draft (Spanish or bilingual)
Certified copy of Founder's passport or national ID
Copy of Foundation Council members' identification
Written appointment of resident agent (abogado/representative)
Evidence of maintained initial endowment subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary or any supervising authority raises technical objections, correct the charter language in accordance with the Notary's instructions and re-execute without additional governmental penalty, provided the defect is remedied within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Foundation Charter with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Foundation Charter through the online registration platform or the physical window of the Public Registry. Attach the power of attorney of the resident attorney and pay the government filing fee. The Registry will examine the document for compliance with Ley No. 25 de 1995.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública)
Notarial certificate of execution (testimonio)
Valid power of attorney in favor of the resident attorney
Payment receipt of the official registration fee
Letter of acceptance from the Foundation Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a 'requerimiento' or query due to omission or illegality, the attorney files a written response and correction within 20 business days. If the Registry rejects the response, appeal to the Director General of the Public Registry within 5 business days; the judicial alternative is a complaint under the Contencioso-Administrativo proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certified Registry Excerpt and Foundation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Certified Copies Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the inscription, request a certified copy of the Foundation Charter (Copia Certificada) and a Certificate of Registration (Certificado de Fundación). Verify that the entity identification (ficha) or foundation number is issued. These documents are mandatory for all subsequent licensing and corporate actions.
required_dossiers: Filing receipt from the Public Registry
Reference number of the inscribed Foundation Charter
Formal written request signed by the resident attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of processing delay or refusal to issue the certificate, file a written petition before the Registro's Director of Certified Copies and request expedited service under the Ley de Simplificación Administrativa.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Foundation for tax purposes and obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) through the DGI online portal. Provide the foundation certificate, charter, and appointed legal representative details. The RUC is required before applying for operating licenses, bank accounts, or import permits.
required_dossiers: Foundation Certificate (Certificado de Fundación)
Certified copy of the Foundation Charter
Copy of legal representative's passport/national ID
Proof of registered office address
DGI Form 901 (inscripción del contribuyente)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI returns a 'reparo' or notice, submit the corrected application within 15 days. If a discrepancy in address or representative status exists, provide a supplementary notarial certificate and request reactivation of the application through the DGI's electronic remedies platform.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Municipal Operating License (Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá (Alcaldía) — Department of Economic Activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the municipal permit application for 'Aviso de Operación Industrial' at the Municipality's one-stop window. Include the RUC, foundation proof, description of manufacturing activity (dental ceramic blocks), and premises information. Payment of municipal tax and annual operation fee is completed at the same time.
required_dossiers: RUC Certificate
Foundation Certificate and certified charter
Description of industrial operations (ISIC 3250)
Lease or title deed for the manufacturing premises
Fire safety clearance or preliminary inspection report
Certificate of zoning compatibility from the Municipal Urban Planning office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality questions zoning or industrial classification, obtain a formal zoning certificate (Certificado de Uso de Suelo) and submit within 10 business days. If the license is denied, the applicant may file a 'recurso de reconsideración' with the Mayor and, subsequently, a 'recurso de apelación' to the Council of the Municipal Government.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Industrial Registration from the Ministry of Commerce and Industries
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — Dirección Nacional de Empresas / Registro Industrial
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the manufacturing facility under the industrial registry applicable to dental consumable manufacturing. This process validates the ISIC code 3250 classification and allows the Foundation to import machinery and claim any industrial tax incentives. The application is filed electronically with the MICI VUE platform.
required_dossiers: Municipal Aviso de Operación
RUC and Foundation Certificate
Process description for zirconia block manufacturing
List of machinery and expected production volume
Proof of environmental EIA approval or filing (as applicable)
Certified diagram of the production facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MICI returns a query or suspends processing, correct the technical dossier and resubmit within 10 days. Recurring denials may be addressed by requesting a technical visit and submitting a business plan amendment. Final denial is subject to administrative appeal to the Vice-Minister of Commerce within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — Dirección Nacional de Empresas; Municipality of Panama — Economic Activities Department; Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) for medical device import/export compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación Industrial (Municipal) + Registro Industrial (MICI) + Sanitary Registration for Dental Medical Devices. These licenses are mandatory before manufacturing starts.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría II (Moderate Impact) — Requires a Preliminary Environmental Diagnosis (Diagnóstico Ambiental Preliminar) and an approved Environmental Impact Assessment for the proposed production line of zirconia dental blocks.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Decree No. 2 of February 5, 2014 (Control and Prevention of Water Pollution) for effluent discharge limits: pH 6–9, total suspended solids < 35 mg/L, BOD5 < 50 mg/L, COD < 150 mg/L, oils and greases < 10 mg/L. Air emissions must not exceed VOC thresholds specified in Executive Decree No. 1 of 2010; solid waste management must follow Resolución AG-0381-2016 of MiAMBIENTE.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Certificado de Seguridad del Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá) before operations, including structural load inspection for kilns and milling equipment, electrical capacity review, connection to public fire suppression systems; occupational hygiene clearance from MITRADEL (Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral) and CSS medical-risk evaluation for workers exposed to ceramic dust; industrial noise control to below 85 dB during an 8-hour shift.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; operational portal: Sede Electrónica DGI (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa) with the official DGI domain https://www.dgi.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Panamanian Private Interest Foundation (PIF): (1) The resident foundation agent (licensed Panamanian attorney) files the foundation charter in the Registro Público de Panamá under Law 25 of 1995 and obtains the public-inscription certificate evidencing legal personality; (2) the same agent files the Aviso de Operación (Business Operation Notice) with the DGI; (3) the agent submits the inscription certificate, foundation by-laws (estatutos), Panamanian registered address, and identification of officers/directors via the Sede Electrónica portal, authenticated with the agent's advanced digital signature (Firma Electrónica Avanzada), to obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente — for legal entities the RUC is prefixed with 'N' and carries a numeric body and DGI check digit); (4) the RUC application is made in parallel with the ITBMS registration and the application for DGI electronic-invoicing accreditation. Foreign owners and beneficiaries are permitted without local residency or shareholding; the only hard localization requirements are the registered Panamanian agent and a registered address in Panama.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election and no OECD hybrid-mismatch election mechanism are recognized under Panamanian tax law. Statutory elections available to the PIF include: (a) irrevocable election for the Simplified Small Taxpayer Regime under Law 43 of 2016 where annual gross turnover does not exceed B/.36,000; (b) election by the foundation council to activate the Law 25 of 1995 framework so that only Panama-source income falls within the taxable base (territorial scope); (c) filing of a Consulta Previa (advance tax ruling) with the DGI, which creates a binding administrative determination as to the Panama-source or foreign-source characterization of dental zirconia block sales and related CAD/CAM support services.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panamanian VAT-type transfer tax on movable goods and services)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Registration is mandatory when the entity commences commercial operations; there is no general de minimis exemption above that trigger. However, the Simplified Small Taxpayer Regime (Régimen Simplificado de Pequeños Contribuyentes) is available for taxable turnover not exceeding B/.36,000 per annum. The Balboa is pegged 1:1 to the US dollar; Panama issues no physical currency and uses USD for all tax settlements.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory near-real-time electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) applies to general-regime taxpayers. Invoices are issued via DGI-certified software or the DGI web portal and transmitted through web services/API to the DGI's Sede Electrónica, signed with the taxpayer's Firma Electrónica Avanzada. Each invoice is centrally validated and receives a unique fiscal authorization code and correlative number; the DGI issues an automatic acceptance/rejection response (fiscal clearance). Legacy pre-printed CAF paper invoice series are progressively prohibited and are not permitted for mandatory e-invoicing taxpayers. Automotive digital stamping of each invoice is performed by the DGI in this clearance flow.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and qualifying offshore services are zero-rated ITBMS under Article 1058 of the Panamanian Tax Code. For dental CAD/CAM zirconia blocks: (1) the goods must physically depart Panama under an authorized customs export process through SUCA/VUCEA (the national single-window foreign trade platform); (2) legal title must transfer to a non-resident buyer outside Panama; (3) the sale consideration must flow through banking channels and ultimately be credited to a Panamanian account in compliance with FX repatriation rules; and (4) supporting purchase orders, Incoterms, and payment wiring instructions must be retained. Offshore services (e.g., CAD/CAM design files, digital milling support) also qualify for zero-rating when rendered to non-resident customers and economically enjoyed/utilized outside Panama.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación presentada ante SUCA/VUCEA), Bill of Lading or Airway Bill, Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas or equivalent bank-issued credit confirmation evidencing repatriation of export proceeds into Panama)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI Fiscalización conducts retrospective export substantiation audits. Failure to substantiate a zero-rated export results in retroactive reassessment at the standard 7% ITBMS, plus monthly statutory interest and recargo (surcharge), and clawback of any ITBMS input credits or refunds generated by that transaction. Under the Tax Procedure Code (Law 76 of 2019), fraud or deliberate falsification of export documentation carries monetary penalties ranging from 50% to 200% of the tax evaded, in addition to interest and surcharges; criminal tax-fraud liability, including imprisonment, may be pursued under Panama's Criminal Code. The DGI may also administratively suspend the taxpayer's RUC, revoke e-invoicing authorizations, and block future export clearance certificates until amounts are settled.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP). Panama operates a fully dollarized monetary system without a conventional central bank; the SBP, created by Legislative Decree No. 9 of 1998, is the supreme banking and foreign-exchange compliance authority, while Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as the fiscal agent of the Republic.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Unrestricted full convertibility under a United States Dollar legal-tender regime; the national Balboa is coin-only and pegged 1:1 at par. Current-account flows (export settlements, import payments, service fees) and capital-account flows (foundation capital injections, distributions, loan repayments) are freely convertible with no exchange license, no prior-authority approval, and no surrender requirement. Cross-border profit or asset distributions are freely remitted, but a taxable dividend/asset distribution withholding of 10% is triggered under Section 733 of the Panama Fiscal Code unless the underlying income had already been subject to the 10% non-distributed profits tax; the dental block manufacturer should therefore either retain earnings, obtain a certificado de reinversión, or settle the distribution tax before wiring abroad.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. No statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio exist for export receipts; all export proceeds may be retained in USD. The exporter must register the export through the Panama Customs Authority single window using the Declaración Única de Ingreso, evidence the receipts through bank SWIFT credits, and report the taxable export margin under Formulario 709, being mindful that exports are deemed Panamanian-source if title and risk of loss pass within Panamanian territory.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Demand Deposit Account in USD, with trust-titled capacity in the name of the Private Interest Foundation
Operational Account with linked multi-currency companion accounts (USD primary; EUR and CNH companions for trade settlement)
Operational Account with regional dental-distributor creditor connectivity across Central America
Capital Escrow Account and high-volume TT disbursement account for repeated outbound supplier payments to Chinese zirconia powder mills
Privately-managed operational USD account with flexible documentary acceptance for Private Interest Foundation structures
Treasury clearing account for domestic tax and customs payment obligations; weaker for cross-border letter-of-credit issuance

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: MEDIUM-LOW. Panama's deposit-taking monopoly rests with financial institutions licensed by the SBP; non-bank foreign electronic-money institutions such as Wise, Airwallex, and Mberry are not authorized to hold segregated business deposits or to open on-behalf-of accounts for a Panama Private Interest Foundation. The SBP Innovative Activity Hub, established under Resolution SBP 026-2021, permits sandboxed payment-service providers only when sponsored by a licensed Panamanian bank. Consequently, direct EMI boarding of the PIF is LOW viability, while MEDIUM viability exists for card-acquiring settlements and online collections from dental laboratories through a licensed sponsor bank e-money arrangement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Founder and Foundation Council members must generally appear at a physical account-opening interview at Tier-1 banks; at least one council member and the ultimate beneficial owner, the settlor, must attend in person or complete a supervised video-KYC interview before the bank compliance approval committee. Full-remote opening is granted only to repeat institutional clients or low-risk structures pre-vetted by the registered agent; Tier-2 banks, including Towerbank and Global Bank, will accept remote notarized apostilled foundation documents, while Banco General and Banistmo require physical or video double-interview under SBP Agreement 005-2020.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity of the Private Interest Foundation: the list of beneficiaries and protectors is confidential under Foundation Law 25 of 2012, causing banks to treat the vehicle as non-transparent and high-risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled Foundation Charter and Foundation Deed appointing the Foundation Council and Protector; an express Beneficial Ownership Declaration naming every direct and indirect beneficiary and controlling council member; a legal opinion from a Panama-licensed attorney confirming that the PIF is not an opaque trust and carries no bearer-share risk; and a written undertaking to provide continuous identification by reporting any beneficiary change within 30 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unknown source of funds for the capital escrow account: the PIF minimum endowment is USD 10,000 while the intended trade working capital injection exceeds USD 1,000,000, creating a source-of-wealth anomaly.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements and annual audited financial statements of the settlor entity; signed sales-and-purchase contracts or inventory supply agreements evidencing the commercial source of funds; tax-filed records from the settlor home jurisdiction; a notarized bank-source-of-wealth questionnaire; passport copies of the settlor, beneficiaries, and funders; CRS tax identification forms of all underlying recipients; and two professional bank references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: OFAC, UN, EU, and UK sanctions screening flags arising because upstream zirconia powder is sourced from Mainland China and historically intermediated through Hong Kong trading entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Global sanctions screening reports showing negative hits for all owners and counterparties; a trade-line declaration confirming that the Chinese milling-block supplier is a civilian dental-materials exporter with no military or dual-use nexus; purchase orders, packing lists, customs entries, and bills of lading; KYC packs on every counterparty holding 25% or more ownership; and a sworn denial of any Russian, Belarusian, Iranian, North Korean, or Syrian origin goods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border cash-flow destination risk: downstream distributors include Middle Eastern and Latin American jurisdictions perceived as high-intensity money-laundering or sanctioned-corridor territories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103 payment records including Legal Entity Identifiers of payers and payees; master service agreements annotated with ISIC 3250 Y-TZP zirconia block product descriptions; comfort letters from correspondent banks such as Citibank N.A. Panama or JPMorgan Chase New York; end-beneficiary certifications confirming that final recipients are dental clinicians, prosthetic laboratories, and public health ministries; and a post-transaction verification commitment aligned with OFAC-style due diligence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing uses SWIFT MT103 or MT202 wires from the settlor home bank to the PIF USD account at a Panamanian Tier-1 bank, cleared through New York CHIPS or Fedwire correspondents such as Citibank N.A. Panama or the Banco General New York agency. The purpose code and field 70 remittance information must read FOUNDATION CAPITAL ALLOTMENT — ISIC 3250 DENTAL CERAMIC OPERATIONS, and the beneficiary name must exactly match the PIF account title vetted at onboarding. Documentary verification comprises the notarized and apostilled Foundation Charter, the Foundation Council resolution authorizing the capital subscription, source-of-funds bank statements, settlor financial statements if the injection exceeds USD 250,000, a sworn statement of no third-party fungibility, and the registered agent beneficial-ownership attestation. Panama territorial taxation makes such capital injections tax-neutral; however, any injection structured as a shareholder loan above USD 100,000 bearing interest requires loan documentation and triggers 10% withholding on gross interest paid to the non-resident lender under the Fiscal Code.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Two dominant clearing rails apply. First, high-value recurring trade settlements are executed by SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers from the Panamanian operating account to supplier beneficiary banks, cleared directly through New York in USD or via Hong Kong CNH clearing for Mainland Chinese powder suppliers. Second, documentary commercial letters of credit compliant with UCP600 are issued by the Panamanian issuing bank in favor of Chinese or European machinery suppliers for large CAD/CAM milling-center acquisitions, with drafts and full shipping documents. For European export sales, direct SWIFT MT103 transfers are used to Scandinavian clinical-group bank accounts; for Latin American distributors, USD telegraphic transfers or local-currency permitted proxies are used, always accompanied by commercial invoices, packing lists, and the Panama export declaration. All outward payments carry the ISIC 3250 descriptive field and remain subject to SBP payment-transaction monitoring; no capital controls restrict outward remittances.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CNH Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) — one to twelve month tenor, cash-settled in USD against the offshore Chinese Yuan fix, legally permissible without SBP approval because Panama imposes no foreign-exchange controls.
USD/EUR outright forward contracts — plain-vanilla hedging of European machinery and premium zirconia feedstock import exposure.

Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (CCIRS) — USD floating versus CNH fixed used to hedge the interest-rate and currency exposure of a related-party dental-block plant loan, permitted when the foundation end-user genuinely hedges an underlying commercial exposure.
Foreign-exchange swap (FX swap) — spot-starting against forward-leg treasury management between USD, EUR, and CNH under the bank internal swap additive line.

Deliverable USD/CNH swap or forward contracts — permitted solely with a counterparty bank holding an offshore CNY clearing license in Hong Kong or Singapore, with physical CNY delivery through the HKCNY clearing centre.
CME currency futures on USD/CNH and EUR/USD — permitted through a Panamanian broker-dealer pass-through account under a rolling 22-trading-day margin agreement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registry Fee of the Private Interest Foundation (Tasa Anual de la Fundación)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá / Registro de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January of each calendar year; assessed on an annual basis regardless of the foundation’s registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a surcharge of up to USD 100 plus monthly statutory interest; persistent non-payment for at least two consecutive years may lead to administrative suspension and eventual strike-off or cancellation of the foundation’s registry inscription.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Informative Declaration (Declaración Anual Informativa de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Registro de Beneficiario Final
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the close of each fiscal year; for a fiscal year ending 31 December the return is due no later than 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or submitting materially incorrect information may trigger fines up to USD 15,000 and legal restrictions on the disposition of assets, including the inability to deal with registered movable or immovable property.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Private Interest Foundation is not subject to a mandatory statutory audit solely by reason of its status. A certified independent audit becomes obligatory when (i) the Foundation Charter, Regulations, or Administration Agreement expressly requires an audit; (ii) the foundation generates gross Panama-source business income exceeding B/.1,000,000 and the DGI designates it as a taxpayer requiring audited financial statements; or (iii) the foundation elects to have audited records for obtaining third-party financing or complying with its Charter. Foundations engaged exclusively in foreign-source asset holding, investment, and manufacturing activities outside Panama remain audit-exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (NIIF/IFRS) as adopted by the Dirección General de Ingresos; simplified local accounting standards may be used only where permitted for small/medium-scale taxpayers under Panamanian regulations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The foundation must maintain a private Register of Beneficiaries at its registered office in Panama reflecting the founder, foundation council members, protector, guardian, and any beneficiary or class of beneficiaries. Changes in beneficial interest, transfers of foundation positions, and amendments to beneficiary classes must be recorded by the registered agent promptly. Under Law 254 of 2021, the registered agent must electronically confirm the ultimate beneficial owner with the DGI through the annual informative declaration; any change in beneficial ownership or participation in the foundation must be communicated to the registered agent within 30 days so that the DGI registry remains accurate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries (private register, not filed publicly)
Register of Transfers of Foundation Positions and Rights
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 if audit-exempt; 4,000–12,000 if triggered or contractually required
